newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, gold finds support.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, gold finds support.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed Tuesday, with gold prices closing higher, but silver and platinum group metals ending lower.

"Gold looks like its feeling for a bottom, and the rebound into the close may provide a hint that sub-$345 is support, as gold looks to be correlated with real interest rates, rather than just with inflation now," Chase Manhattan New York managing director Dinsa Mehta said.
Gold prices have fallen as U.S. treasury bonds have sold off in recent weeks, even though U.S. inflation remains low, analysts noted.

U.S. February housing starts jumped 12.2 percent to their highest levels in three years Tuesday, but US treasury bonds found some support, as did gold prices, ahead of the U.S. February CPI data due Wednesday.
Expectations are for only a small 0.2 percent rise in the U.S. February CPI core rate, excluding food and energy, leaving the annual rate still around 2.6 percent, the lowest level since the 1960's.
COMEX April gold ended up $2.10 at $350.10 an ounce, after sliding early to an 18 day low at $346.30. Estimated total volume was a high 70,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $349.20/70, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $346.30 and the New York close Monday around $347.50/50.
Before retreating this week, gold prices had recovered to $365 an ounce, from three year lows at $336.00, as funds reduced near-record net short positions, according to the latest CFTC data.
But concern about rising bond yields, producer hedging, and Switzerland's move to more actively manage its gold had tempted some traders to resume shorting gold, analysts said.

Silver failed to benefit from the rebound in gold Tuesday though, with COMEX May silver slipping below month-old support around $5.200 to a session low at $5.115, before ending down 3.5 cents at $5.190 an ounce.
Platinum group metals also failed to benefit from gold's rebound, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread ending at $27.90 an ounce, down sharply from $33.30 Monday.
NYMEX April platinum closed down $4.40 an ounce at $378.00, while NYMEX June was palladium ended down $5.05 at $145.50 an ounce, after falling the daily limit of $6.00 early on fund selling.
Estimated total volume of 3,073 lots for NYMEX palladium was high for the usually lightly traded instrument.

Spot palladium closed quoted around $142.50 an ounce, aftter falling nearly $10.00 an ounce this week on talk of Russia resuming palladium shipments to Japan which have been halted since the end of 1996.
Earlier spot palladium prices rose about 35 percent in the first two months of the year to around $160 an ounce, the highest level since June 1995, on the disruption to Russian supplies.

"Palladium is probably still good value, as we expect Russian palladium exports this year to be down 10-15 percent on last year, while we are revising up our estimates of auto sector demand," CPM Group analyst Ted Kempf said.
